correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all twenty words by dihedral symmetry, verifies two full characteristic-polynomial differences and common determinants exactly, bounds Perron roots by one-third traces, and applies the sign of the cubic above its spectral radius to prove strict inequalities on the complete open parameter domain. The rational example uses an explicit positive subeigenvector and a negative exact determinant; checker.py independently verifies each algebraic identity and witness from the packaged file.

originality.rationale: The claim is a new exact all-word ordering within the inspected literature: the two primary temporal-SIS publications prove general product thresholds but neither states or proves the universal three-class inequalities and rational sign-changing example. The only close six-word comparison in accessible historical claims concerns noncommuting two-dimensional continuous-time exposed/infective progression factors, gives the reverse ordering, and does not imply a result for the specified three-dimensional nonnegative edge-switch factors. A separate four-season two-patch ecological comparison neither contains nor implies the present six-season statement. Priority beyond inspected sources remains provisional, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The twenty schedules are a complete naturally defined finite family of equal aggregate contact counts, and the strict rate-uniform ordering establishes an exact best and worst pattern for linear SIS invasion. The exact rational threshold-crossing instance proves aggregation can give conflicting outbreak-linearization decisions. This is a motivated temporal-network epidemiology boundary, not a renaming of the generic infection-propagator formula; applicability is restricted to the specified mean-field path.
